title: What setup and an edit may save: a schedule change never before its latest settled or named occurrence, a goal's own account in the home currency, setup's not-yet questions (X8, W3, X3)
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 sections 4, 5 and 8 (the opening); DECISIONS_ROUND2 X3, X8, W3, AB3 (the last statement asked at setup; AD6 and AD7: "no" asks the amount with everything owed filled in, "don't know" on a loan or pay-later is that month's usual payment; AE6: the question asked as "Has your last card statement already left your bank?", an automatic debit not yet until it comes out; AF2: "no" on a loan or pay-later filled with the usual payment) and AB with MAKO M1 (the minimum asked once, box empty); AH2 (X8 reads moved schedule ids: `mv:pay:steps.a@...`, `pe:mv:...`, `ps:mv:...`) and AH3 (keyed overrides in the AE1 shape; a removed key names nothing), AJ5, AK2 and AK3 (one-off amounts and `once` keys in the way offered to move or remove) and AL6 (no occurrence of the new rule left in that month: the next one; two landing on one occurrence: the offer shows both, add or replace)
notes: Hand-worked cases for edit-time and setup rules that the reference model does not hold [H7]. All amounts and dates are made up.

cases.title: A pay day change dated before a settled pay is refused; the edit offers the day after it (X8, c8)
cases.why: The latest settled occurrence of the pay is pay@2026-12-10 (rent's settle is another schedule's). 1 Dec is on or before it, so the change would rename or remove a settled pay [X8]: refused, and the edit offers Fri 11 Dec, the first day after it.

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: A change dated after every settled pay is saved as asked (X8)
cases.why: 1 Jan 2027 is after pay@2026-12-10, the latest settled occurrence, so nothing settled or named is rewritten [X8, H2].

cases.why: On or before: a change from 10 Dec would own the 10 Dec occurrence [H2], so it is refused and 11 Dec offered [X8].

cases.why: `amounts` names pay@2027-01-10 (keyed by its due date). A change from 5 Jan would make that key name nothing [X8]: refused, 11 Jan offered. The key is in the AE1 shape, `{ amount, at, by }` [AE1, AH3]. Only the one-off amount of 10 Jan is in the way (the 10 Dec settle is before 5 Jan), so the edit also offers to move or remove it [AJ5].

Nothing that cannot move is in the way (the settled pay is 10 Feb), so the key is offered to move or remove [AK3]; no new rule is given, so no day to move it to is named.

cases.question: not_yet_asks
cases.title: Setup asks about pay and bills due from the last pay to the setup day, a pay due that day first (X3, F20)
cases.why: Asked: what is due after the last pay (25 May, already in) up to and including the setup day, Fri 25 Jun [X3]. The pay due that day is asked first; the rest by due date. Rent of 27 Jun is after setup and is simply expected.

cases.question: not_yet_asks
cases.title: Nothing due since the last pay: setup asks nothing (X3)
cases.why: Nothing is due between the last pay and the setup day, so there is nothing to ask [X3].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AB3: a card set up between its close and its payment day is asked "Is the last statement paid?"; yes is saved as a paid statement
cases.why: The card closes on the last day and is paid on the 27th of the next month. Setup on Fri 20 Nov falls after the close of Sat 31 Oct and before its payment day, Fri 27 Nov, so setup asks [AB3]. Yes: a statement check for the 31 Oct close, paid; no amount is asked. Everything owed now is after that close. The question is asked as "Has your last card statement already left your bank?" [AE6].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AB3, AD6: answered no: the amount box opens with everything owed filled in; the person types the statement's amount
cases.why: No, not paid: setup asks the amount with everything owed, 50,000, filled in [AD6]; the person changes it to the October statement, 30,000: saved as an unpaid statement closed 31 Oct and paid 27 Nov [AB3, J5]. Of the 50,000 owed, 50,000 - 30,000 = 20,000 is November so far. The question is asked as "Has your last card statement already left your bank?" [AE6].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AB3: answered don't know: everything owed is that statement, due on the next payment day
cases.why: "Don't know" counts everything owed as due on the next payment day [AB3]: the statement saved holds all 50,000 owed and is paid on Fri 27 Nov (the safe side, as H4). The question is asked as "Has your last card statement already left your bank?" [AE6].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AB3: set up after the payment day and before the next close: not asked (X6 holds)
cases.why: Sat 28 Nov is after the 27 Nov payment day of the October statement and before the next close, Mon 30 Nov. There is no statement waiting between its close and its payment day, so nothing is asked; the first close after the opening holds what is owed [X6].

cases.question: min_ask
cases.title: Mako M1: setup asks "Keep at least ___ in your bank?" with the box empty; skipping means no minimum
cases.why: The box starts empty (no amount filled in for the person) and they skip it: `home.main` holds `min: null`, no minimum [AB, MAKO M1]. The main bank's own `minBank` stays null [AN3].

cases.question: min_ask
cases.title: Mako M1: a typed minimum is kept in the home currency
cases.why: The person types 20,000: `home.main` holds `min:` { a: 20,000, cur: JPY } [AB, MAKO M1, O6]. The main bank's own `minBank` stays null [AN3].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AD6: answered no and the filled-in amount left as it is: everything owed is that statement
cases.why: No, not paid: the amount box opens with everything owed, 50,000 [AD6]. The person leaves it, so the unpaid statement closed Sat 31 Oct holds 50,000, all due on Fri 27 Nov; 50,000 - 50,000 = 0 is November so far. Before AD6 a "no" with no amount typed saved no amount (ed-q1). The question is asked as "Has your last card statement already left your bank?" [AE6].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AD7: a loan answered don't know: that month's usual payment is due on the next payment day, not the whole balance
cases.why: A loan of 400,000 paying 20,000 a month on the 27th, set up Fri 20 Nov, between its statement (Sat 31 Oct) and its payment day (Fri 27 Nov), so setup asks [AB3]. "Don't know" on a loan means that month's usual payment, 20,000, is due on Fri 27 Nov [AD7], not the whole 400,000 owed. 400,000 - 20,000 = 380,000 stays owed after it. The question is asked as "Has your last card statement already left your bank?" [AE6].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AD7: a pay-later answered don't know: that month's usual payment
cases.why: A pay-later owing 30,000, paying 10,000 a month on the 27th, set up Fri 20 Nov: "don't know" means that month's usual payment, 10,000, is due on Fri 27 Nov [AD7]; 30,000 - 10,000 = 20,000 stays owed. The question is asked as "Has your last card statement already left your bank?" [AE6].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AF2: a loan answered "no, not paid": the amount is asked, filled with that month's usual payment
cases.why: A car loan owing 400,000, paying 20,000 a month on the 27th, set up Fri 20 Nov between its statement (Sat 31 Oct) and its payment day (Fri 27 Nov), so setup asks [AB3, AE6]. Answered no: the amount is asked, the box filled with that month's usual payment, 20,000, not everything owed [AF2]; left as it is, 20,000 is due on 27 Nov and 400,000 - 20,000 = 380,000 stays owed after it.

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AF2: a pay-later answered "no, not paid": the box filled with the usual payment; the typed amount is saved
cases.why: A pay-later owing 45,000 in three parts of 15,000, set up Fri 20 Nov between its statement (Sat 31 Oct) and its payment day (Fri 27 Nov). Answered no: the box opens with that month's usual payment, 15,000 [AF2]; the person changes it to the 12,000 the statement says, and that is saved, due on 27 Nov [AB3, J5].

cases.question: statement_ask
cases.title: AE6: a card paid by automatic debit, set up before the debit day: "not yet", so the statement is still due
cases.why: A Japanese card closing on the last day, paid by automatic debit on the 27th of the next month; set up Fri 20 Nov. The question is "Has your last card statement already left your bank?", with the line that an automatic debit counts as not yet until the day it comes out [AE6]. The October statement comes out on Fri 27 Nov, so the answer is not yet (the saved answer is the same as "no"): the box opens with everything owed, 50,000 [AD6]; the person types the statement's 30,000: unpaid, due 27 Nov. Of the 50,000, 50,000 - 30,000 = 20,000 is November so far. Read the old way ("is it paid?" meaning "will it be paid?") the answer was yes and the 30,000 was never counted until the debit landed (confirm_review_3, watch).

A change from 1 Dec would leave that key naming an occurrence the new rule might not make [X8]; a moved schedule is protected like any other [AH2]: refused, 26 Jan offered (the day after 2027-01-25). Before AH2 the occurrence name `mv:pay:steps.a@2027-01-25` did not match the name pattern and the change was allowed. Only the one-off amount of 25 Jan is in the way, so the edit also offers to move or remove it [AJ5].

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: AJ5: a December bonus set on the pay stops a new employer's pay day; the edit offers to move or remove it (confirm_review_5 h1, WATCH)
cases.why: December's pay was set to 400,000 with a bonus (a one-off `amounts` key, not settled). The person changes jobs: the new employer pays on the 10th from 1 Dec. The key names 25 Dec, on or after 1 Dec, so the change alone is refused, offering Sat 26 Dec [X8]. The only thing in the way is a future one-off amount of the pay itself, so the edit also offers to move that amount (to the new pay day's first occurrence in December, ed-45 [AK2]) or remove it [AJ5]; either one lets the change start on 1 Dec. Refusing only, the person could not enter the new pay day.

cases.why: The 25 Dec pay is settled, so no change can start on or before it [X8]; moving or removing January's amount would not let 1 Dec through, so it is not offered [AJ5]. The latest named occurrence is 25 Jan: the edit offers Tue 26 Jan.

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: AJ5: two future one-off amounts are both offered
cases.why: A December bonus (400,000) and January's unpaid leave (0) are both one-off amounts of the pay, not settled, on or after 1 Dec. The latest is 25 Jan, so the change alone is refused, offering Tue 26 Jan [X8]; moving or removing both lets it start on 1 Dec, so both are offered, by date [AJ5].

cases.why: December's pay names an answered period too (`pe:`), which cannot be moved: moving the bonus would not free the day, so only the refusal and its offer are given [X8, AJ5, T1].

cases.title: AK2: the December bonus moves to the new pay day's first occurrence in December, Thu 10 Dec
cases.why: As ed-40: December's pay was set to 400,000 with a bonus, and the new employer pays on the 10th from Tue 1 Dec. The new rule's occurrences in December on or after 1 Dec are 10 Dec only, so "move" puts the 400,000 on Thu 10 Dec [AK2]. December then has one pay, 400,000 on 10 Dec, where it had 400,000 on 25 Dec: the month's income is the same, 15 days sooner. The settled 25 Nov pay is untouched.

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: AK2: two one-off amounts each move within their own month
cases.why: As ed-42: a December bonus (400,000) and January's unpaid leave (0). With the new pay day the 10th from 1 Dec, each moves to the first occurrence of the new rule in its own month [AK2]: the bonus to Thu 10 Dec, the 0 to Sun 10 Jan (named by its due date before any move for the weekend [H2]). December gets 400,000, January 0 from this pay, as before the change.

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: AK2: every other Friday: each amount goes to the first Friday pay of its month, not the nearest
cases.why: The new employer pays every other Friday from Fri 4 Dec: 4 Dec, 18 Dec, 1 Jan, 15 Jan, 29 Jan (4 + 14 = 18; 18 + 14 = 32, so 1 Jan; 15; 29). The bonus of 25 Dec goes to the first occurrence in December, 4 Dec, though 18 Dec is nearer to 25 Dec [AK2]; the 0 of 25 Jan goes to 1 Jan (named by its due date before the New Year move [H2]), though 29 Jan is nearer. December: 400,000 on 4 Dec plus the usual pay on 18 Dec; January: 0 on 1 Jan, the usual on 15 and 29 Jan.

cases.title: AK3: a budget line's and the share's `once` keys named by the December pay move with the bonus
cases.why: With the December bonus the person set Food to 60,000 for the period of the 25 Dec pay (a budget line's `once` key) and 30,000 more for Free to spend (the share's `once` key) for Christmas. All three are named by the 25 Dec pay, none settled [AK3, AJ5]. With the new pay day the 10th from 1 Dec, "move" puts the bonus on 10 Dec and both keys on the period that pay starts, `k7qzpa-m2xq7ab9zt-41@2026-12-10` [AK2, AK3]: that period gets the 400,000, Food 60,000 and the extra 30,000, as the 25 Dec one would have. "Remove" takes all three away.

cases.title: AK3: a share's `once` key alone is offered, and moves to the first Friday pay of December
cases.why: The person gives 20,000 more in the period of the 25 Dec pay (the share's `once` key, `give`). The new employer pays every other Friday from 4 Dec. The key is the only thing in the way: refused, offering Sat 26 Dec, and offered to move or remove [AK3]; "move" puts it on the first occurrence in December, Fri 4 Dec [AK2], so the period from 4 Dec gives 20,000 more.

cases.why: The 25 Dec pay names an answered period-end (`pe:`), which cannot be moved, so moving the Food key would not free the day: only the refusal and its offer [X8, AK3, as AJ5 in ed-44].

cases.title: AK3: a removed `once` key names nothing and is not offered; the bonus still is
cases.why: The Food key for the 25 Dec period was removed at 11:00 (`gone`), so it names nothing [AH3]: only the bonus is in the way and only the bonus is offered, to Thu 10 Dec [AK2].

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: AL6: no occurrence of the new pay day left in December: the bonus goes to the next one, Sun 10 Jan
cases.why: The December bonus (400,000) is keyed 25 Dec. The new job starts on Tue 15 Dec and pays on the 10th. December's only occurrence of the new rule is 10 Dec, before 15 Dec, so there is none in December on or after the change; the bonus goes to the new rule's next occurrence, Sun 10 Jan (named by its due date before any weekend move [H2]) [AL6]. Before AL6 the reference gave null here and the bonus could only be removed (ed-q1). The change alone is still refused, offering Sat 26 Dec [X8].

cases.question: change_from
cases.title: AL6: two amounts land on 10 Jan: the offer shows both and the person picks add or replace
cases.why: As ed-52 with January's unpaid leave (0, keyed 25 Jan) too. The bonus has no December occurrence on or after 15 Dec, so it goes to the next, 10 Jan [AL6]; January's 0 goes to the first January occurrence on or after 15 Dec, also 10 Jan [AK2]. Two amounts land on one day: the offer shows both (400,000 and 0) and the person picks add (400,000 + 0 = 400,000 on 10 Jan) or replace [AL6]. The reference lists them in date order under `together`, with `togetherOffer`; nothing is added up until the person picks.

cases.title: AL6: twice a month to once a month: the 10 Dec amount moves onto 25 Dec, which already has its own: add or replace
cases.why: The pay came on the 10th and the 25th; December's two pays were set to 200,000 (10 Dec, with a bonus) and 180,000 (25 Dec). From Tue 1 Dec the employer pays once, on the 25th. Each amount goes to the first December occurrence on or after 1 Dec, 25 Dec [AK2]: the 10 Dec amount lands on 25 Dec, which already has its own 180,000. The offer shows both and the person picks add (200,000 + 180,000 = 380,000 on 25 Dec) or replace [AL6]. The change alone is refused, offering Sat 26 Dec [X8].

cases.title: AL6: two budget-line `once` keys land on the period of the 10 Jan pay: add or replace
cases.why: Food is set to 60,000 for the period of the 25 Dec pay and to 50,000 for the period of the 25 Jan pay (`once` keys [B8, T1]). The new job pays on the 10th from 15 Dec. The December key has no December occurrence on or after 15 Dec, so it goes to the next, the 10 Jan pay [AL6]; the January key to the first January occurrence on or after 15 Dec, the same 10 Jan pay [AK2, AK3]. Both name one period: the offer shows both (60,000 and 50,000) and the person picks add (110,000) or replace [AL6].

cases.question: min_save
cases.title: AN3: the main bank's minimum is saved only in `home.main`; the account's own `minBank` stays null
cases.why: The person raises "Keep at least" on the main bank from 20,000 to 30,000. The main bank's minimum lives only in `home.main` [AN3, AL3]: the pair is written with the new minimum and a new `at`; the account's own `minBank` is null and stays null, so the figure is in one place (LESSONS lesson 1).

cases.question: min_save
cases.title: AN3: another account's minimum is its own `minBank`; `home.main` is not touched
cases.why: The person sets a 5,000 minimum on the e-wallet. It is not the main bank, so its minimum is its own `minBank`, in its currency [AN3, O6]; `home.main` is unchanged.

cases.question: min_ok
cases.title: AN3: a copy whose main bank carries its own `minBank` is refused
cases.why: The main bank's own `minBank` is always null; its minimum lives only in `home.main` [AN3]. A copy holding 10,000 on the account and 20,000 in `home.main` has one figure in two places, so it is refused, as X8 refuses a copy a change made unsound.

cases.question: min_ok
cases.title: AN3: the main bank's `minBank` null and another account with its own minimum: sound
cases.why: The main bank's minimum is in `home.main` (20,000) and its own `minBank` is null; the e-wallet's 5,000 is its own [AN3].

cases.question: move_save
cases.title: AN5: two amounts moved onto one pay: January's own is written, December's waits in `pendingMove` until the person picks add or replace; nothing unpicked is saved in `amounts`
cases.why: As ed-53 with January's 150,000 (part unpaid leave). Wed 2 Dec 10:00 the person picks move: December's 400,000 bonus goes to 10 Jan (no December occurrence of the new rule on or after 15 Dec, AL6) and January's 150,000 to 10 Jan (the first January one, AK2). Both old keys are removed by their own `gone` with the edit's `at`. January's amount is 10 Jan's own (the same month), so it is written there. December's lands on an occurrence that now has its own amount, so it is not written until the person picks add or replace: it waits in `pendingMove`, an ordinary record (`waits: 'pick'`, the schedule, the target key, where it came from, the amount) [AN5]. Until then it counts nowhere (section 2.1), and no `pick` key exists.

cases.question: move_save

cases.why: The rent of moved_together: 80,000 on the 27th, December's set to 95,000 (a repair) and January's to 70,000 (a discount). Wed 2 Dec 10:00 the new flat's rent is on the 5th from 15 Dec and the person picks move. 5 Jan had no amount of its own. December's has no December 5th on or after 15 Dec, so it goes to the next, 5 Jan [AL6]; January's goes to the first January 5th, the same day [AK2]. Of the two, the one from 5 Jan's own month, January's 70,000, is its own and is written [AO2]; December's 95,000 waits in `pendingMove` for add or replace [AN5]. The order the two are listed in does not matter: December's is listed first here.

cases.question: main_change
cases.title: AO5: the e-wallet becomes the main bank: its own minimum moves into `home.main` and is cleared; the old main bank gets none, with a notice

notices.text: This account is no longer your main bank, so it has no minimum now. Set one if you want to keep some money in it.

cases.why: The bank is the main bank with "keep at least" 20,000 (in `home.main`, AN3); the e-wallet keeps its own 5,000. Tue 1 Dec 09:00 the person makes the e-wallet the main bank. Its own 5,000 moves into `home.main` with it, written as the pair with a new `at` [AO5, AL3], and its `minBank` is cleared (null, with the same `at`), so the figure is in one place [AN3]. The bank's 20,000 does not follow it back: the bank's own `minBank` stays null, and a notice says the old main bank has no minimum now [AO5].

open.question: AO4 makes a budget line's or a share's `once` key wait in `pendingMove` like an amount (ed-65 to ed-68), and AO3 says how a waiting bill or pay amount counts in the walk. Does a waiting `once` amount count on the safe side until the pick (the larger keeps more aside for Food in that period, less to spend now), or nowhere?
open.ref_does: Counts nowhere until picked: the look ahead reads only `to: 'amounts'` entries (AO3); the period keeps the amount written on its key.
